analysis.investment_thesis: PhysicsWallah is a genuine growth story with 131% revenue CAGR and a founder-visionary in Alakh Pandey who disrupted Indian EdTech through social media reach — exactly the kind of innovative distribution Fisher admires. However, the company has not yet proven it can convert explosive revenue growth into durable profits, and at 433x EV/EBITDA the market has already priced in a decade of flawless execution.
key_strengths: Explosive revenue growth: 233 → 2,887 Cr in 3 years (131% CAGR) with operating CF positive all 4 years — the business generates real cash while scaling
Visionary founder-led management: Alakh Pandey built a massive organic distribution moat via YouTube/social media before monetizing — rare and authentic market penetration
Operational recovery in FY2025: EBITDA turned positive at 234 Cr and FCF surged to 340 Cr after heavy investment years, suggesting the expansion phase is yielding returns
key_risks: Profitability unproven at scale: Net loss of -243 Cr in FY2025 (after a catastrophic -1,131 Cr in FY2024); ROE of -17% signals equity still being destroyed
Capital allocation red flag: The -672 Cr 'other income' in FY2024 almost certainly reflects acquisition/investment write-downs — raises serious questions about management's M&A discipline
Valuation demands perfection: At 433x EV/EBITDA and 99.68x forward P/E, any growth deceleration or margin disappointment could cause severe de-rating
red_flags: FY2024 other income of -672 Cr suggests major impairment of acquired assets — management overpaid on acquisitions
Equity swung from +106 Cr (2022) to -1,246 Cr (2024) before being recapitalized via IPO — the company burned through capital at a dangerous rate
Borrowings spiked to 2,461 Cr in FY2024 before being partially repaid; financing costs rose to 85 Cr, pressuring a loss-making P&L
analysis.detailed_analysis:
PhysicsWallah's revenue growth of 131% CAGR is the kind of number that would immediately capture Fisher's attention — this is not incremental growth but market disruption. The hybrid offline/online model targeting India's enormous JEE, NEET, and UPSC prep market addresses a genuine, durable TAM. Operating cash flow has been positive every single year despite heavy expansion, which Fisher would note as a mark of a business model with real economic substance beneath the accounting losses. The FY2025 recovery — EBITDA at 234 Cr vs. -161 Cr in FY2024, FCF at 340 Cr — suggests the worst of the investment phase is behind the company.

However, Fisher's scuttlebutt method would surface serious concerns. The -672 Cr "other income" charge in FY2024 is almost certainly goodwill impairment from acquisitions, indicating management paid too much for inorganic growth — a capital allocation failure Fisher would weigh heavily. The stock's valuation at 433x EV/EBITDA assumes the company will compound earnings at extraordinary rates for many years with no stumbles. Fisher tolerated high P/E multiples for genuinely superior businesses, but he also required confidence in management's financial discipline, which is not yet established here. The turnaround in FY2025 is encouraging but one year of improvement does not overcome a track record of losses and write-downs. This is a WATCH closely, buy on further proof of profitability.
